concept.name: Buy and hold
concept.definition: A passive investment strategy of purchasing securities - typically diversified equity funds - and holding them for years regardless of short-term price fluctuations, forgoing timing decisions in favor of long-run participation in asset growth. Positions are selected once and traded only for rebalancing, contributions, or withdrawals.
concept.intuition: If you cannot reliably predict next month's price, own productive assets and let compounding and time in the market do the work; every round trip avoided is costs and taxes not paid.
concept.mechanics: Acquire the chosen assets and hold through bull and bear markets; capital-gains taxes are deferred until sale, and turnover and transaction costs approach zero. Indexed implementations hold constituents as long as they remain in the index, with annual turnover often under 5%.
concept.failure_modes: Secular bear markets or buying at extreme valuations can produce a decade or more of flat real returns, and behavioral failure - panic selling at the bottom - converts a temporary drawdown into a permanent loss.
concept.misconceptions: That buy and hold means never reassessing; the strategy concerns trading frequency, not due diligence - holdings still require periodic review for thesis or allocation drift, and long-run equity outperformance is a historical pattern, not a law.
concept.example: 100 shares of Apple bought at $18 in January 2008 and held to January 2019 (then $157) returned nearly 900% over 11 years without a single trade (Investopedia example).
